:::{#thm-pois-two-group-mle}
#### Poisson regression estimates for two groups

Suppose we fit the Poisson regression model (@def-poisson-reg)
$\eta(x) = \b_0 + \b_1 x$
with a single binary covariate $x \in \cb{0, 1}$
to independent observations $(y_i, x_i, t_i)$, $i = 1, \lds, n$.
For each group $k \in \cb{0, 1}$,
let

$$
D_k \eqdef \sum_{i: x_i = k} y_i,
\qquad
T_k \eqdef \sum_{i: x_i = k} t_i
$$

be the group's total event count and total exposure,
and suppose $D_0 > 0$, $D_1 > 0$, $T_0 > 0$, and $T_1 > 0$.
Then the [maximum likelihood estimates](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle)
of the two event rates are the groups' crude event rates:

$$
\el(0) = \expf{\eb_0} = \frac{D_0}{T_0},
\qquad
\el(1) = \expf{\eb_0 + \eb_1} = \frac{D_1}{T_1}
$$

so the estimated rate ratio is the ratio of the crude rates:

$$
\erateratio(1 : 0) = \expf{\eb_1} = \frac{D_1 / T_1}{D_0 / T_0}
$$ {#eq-pois-two-group-rr}

:::
